newsitem.title: INDIA: Moopanar is odds-on favourite with Indian punters.
newsitem.headline: Moopanar is odds-on favourite with Indian punters.

text.p: Indian bookies are betting that regional leader G.K. Moopanar will lead the next government, but have not ruled out the prospect of caretaker Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral pipping him at the post.

Indians who placed bets said illegal bookmakers were offering odds of 1:4 that Moopanar, who defected from the Congress party last year to form a party in southern Tamil Nadu, would succeed Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Deve Gowda resigned last Friday after his centre-left coalition lost a parliamentary vote of confidence.
With odds of 1:5, Gujral was closing in on Moopanar, according to bookies in Kucha Mahajani, Delhi's old quarter where the most hectic betting is usually concentrated.
"The general bent in the United Front constituents seems to be in favour of Moopanar; that's why the odds are in his favour," said Ram Prasad Jaiswal, who described himself as a habitual punter.
Although gambling is illegal, except on horse racing at the course, many Indians wager regularly, often in large amounts.
Cricket, the national passion, draws the most money, with some spectators at a major match even betting on each ball.
Elections draw huge bets. Bookies are coy when it comes to how big election business is, but hundreds of millions of rupees (millions of U.S. dollars) are likely to be bet on the outcome.
Bookmakers said Gujral's chances had brightened considerably in the last few days.
"Gujral has impeccable credentials, a spotless image and also has experience of governance as ambassador and foreign minister," said Jaiswal.

Further back in the pack were communist leader Jyoti Basu at 1:20, Bihar state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav at 1:70, Congress president Sitaram Kesri at 1:90 and Bharatiya Janata Party leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee at 1:100.
Punters were unanimous that the country was heading for mid-term elections, but not immediately.
"Mid-term elections are certainly in the cards, all this talk about a new leader is because the parties want to get the budget out of the way," Jaiswal added.
Punters said another surprise candidate could be former prime minister Chandrashekhar. The odds offered on Chandrashekhar are 1:23, and improving steadily.
"Today Deve Gowda met Chandrashekhar, so you never know if Chandrashekhar might end up becoming the next prime minister," said Pandit, who declined to give his full name.
